language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

translation.text:
<meta>Woodblock-printed folio in faded red ink inside a double-ruled frame. The scan is rotated 90°. The Mongolian body text could not be read reliably and was not transcribed, so there is nothing in it to translate. The red number "299" is a digitization overlay and not part of the printed page.</meta>

<margin>Secret Tantra section, volume 5, upper, folio 290 <note>original Chinese margin label: "秘密經第五卷上二百九十". "Secret Scriptures" (秘密經) is the Chinese name for the Tantra section, Mongolian <term>Dandir-a</term> <gloss>Tantra</gloss>, of the Mongolian Kanjur. "Upper" probably marks the front side of the folio.</note></margin>

<unclear>about 23 lines of Classical Mongolian text in Uighur-Mongol script (faded red woodblock print), not transcribed</unclear>

<summary>This page is folio 290 of volume 5 in the Tantra section of a woodblock-printed Mongolian Kanjur, the Buddhist canon in Mongolian. Only the Chinese margin label could be read and translated. The roughly 23 lines of Mongolian text were not transcribed, so their content is unknown.</summary>
